summary.headline: First new trading session (Mon 2026-07-06) since Thursday 7/2 brought a broad risk-on rally — a weaker-than-expected June jobs report (57K vs ~113K forecast) cooled Fed rate-hike fears and reversed most of the prior AI-capex-fear chip selloff. CRDO (+9.71%, fresh Evercore/Stifel/BofA upgrades) and AMD (+6.56%, Goldman PT to $640) are RESOLVED to green. LRCX, MRVL, HUT, MARA and KEYS all downgrade RED→AMBER on stabilization/recovery with no new negative catalyst (though LRCX notably didn't participate in the rally, and its CEO disclosed an $11.7M stock sale). AEM is now the lone RED: no new operational news, but analysts split (Jefferies upgrade vs UBS cut) while the Barnat guidance-cut risk stays open until the formal Q2 update on 7/29. QCOM holds AMBER as Citi's new 30-day downside catalyst watch (citing a ~30% Xiaomi 2026 shipment-forecast cut) gives the first concrete confirmation of the already-flagged Chinese-handset-softness risk. FTNT holds AMBER, unchanged. Headline roster item: CWAN is now fully deregistered (Form 15-12G filed 7/6) yet still sits in portfolios.json's growth sleeve — 8th consecutive run flagging this. LMT's Ultra Maritime interest converted from rumor to a signed $3.45B definitive agreement.
summary.prior_session_note: Markets were closed/quiet Fri 7/3 (Independence Day observed) through the weekend; today's drop reflects the first real new session (Mon 7/6) since Thu 7/2.

flags.headline: AEM +0.74% — persisting RED: Barnat guidance-cut risk still unresolved; analysts split (Jefferies upgrade vs UBS cut)
flags.detail: No new operational or geotechnical disclosure since the original 2026-07-01 release: a rock-mass wall movement on the Barnat open pit's north wall (Canadian Malartic, Quebec) forced a precautionary suspension of in-pit mining there — no injuries/equipment damage/environmental impact. Agnico still expects H2 2026 production down ~60,000-80,000 oz, with 2027-2028 production potentially reduced up to ~150,000 oz/year pending an ongoing geotechnical assessment; formal updated guidance is due with Q2 2026 results, after market close 2026-07-29. New this run: analysts split on 2026-07-06 — Jefferies upgraded AEM to Buy (PT $200, from $187) while UBS cut its PT to $170 (from $210) but kept Neutral. Price is essentially stable (+0.74% to $155.04), which is not evidence the underlying execution-miss risk has resolved — it stays RED until the formal guidance update.
flags.thesis_link: Matches AEM key_risk: "any execution miss on the 4M+ oz production target ... could trigger meaningful valuation compression" — a confirmed multi-year production cut at a flagship asset is that execution-miss risk materializing.

flags.headline: HUT +6.77% — downgraded RED→AMBER: sector-wide AI-pivot-miner rally (TeraWulf-Anthropic $19B lease), BTC itself soft
flags.detail: Rallied on 2026-07-06 alongside the rest of the bitcoin-mining/AI-infrastructure group after TeraWulf signed a 20-year, ~$19B/~400MW lease with Anthropic in Kentucky — not a Hut 8-specific catalyst, but a validating comp for Hut 8's own $16.8B AI-infrastructure lease backlog and Anthropic capacity deal. No new Hut 8-specific SEC filing (last 8-K dated 2026-06-12). Bitcoin itself was soft/mixed the same session (opened ~$63,590, slipped into the $61,700-$63,900 range, pressured partly by Strategy/MSTR selling 3,588 BTC) — so the rally reflects AI-infra sector sentiment, not crypto-market strength. Treasury (~10,278 BTC) unchanged. Downgrading given no new negative development, but the core BTC-price-exposure risk is unchanged and the underlying asset was weak even as the stock rallied.
flags.thesis_link: Matches HUT key_risk: "Bitcoin price exposure remains significant ... demonstrate the volatility of the crypto treasury strategy."

flags.headline: QCOM +5.87% — persisting AMBER: Citi's downside catalyst watch (Xiaomi 2026 shipment cut ~30%) is the first concrete confirmation of the China-handset-softness key_risk
flags.detail: Stock rallied to $186.47 on 2026-07-06 alongside Benchmark's reaffirmed Buy ($300 PT), part of the same broad chip/AI rebound lifting the whole sector after a weak June jobs report cooled rate-hike fears. Working the other direction: Citi placed QCOM on a 30-day downside catalyst watch the same day, citing reports that Xiaomi cut its 2026 shipment forecast by ~30% — the first concrete data point tying directly to the already-flagged 'Chinese customer weakness' key_risk (Q2 FY2026 QCT China revenue -4.2% YoY). Separately, single-sourced and date-imprecise reporting (Simply Wall St) suggests QCOM is in advanced talks to acquire AI-infrastructure software firm Modular Inc. for ~$4B — flagged as unverified/tentative pending a primary source. Net: today's price strength is sector-wide, not company-specific; the Xiaomi data point is a real, if partial, thesis-risk confirmation, so this stays AMBER rather than resolving.
flags.thesis_link: Matches QCOM key_risk: "Chinese customer weakness drove Q2 FY2026 QCT revenue down 4.2% YoY" — Citi's downside-catalyst watch citing a ~30% Xiaomi 2026 shipment-forecast cut is the first concrete signal since screening that this risk may continue into 2H2026.

evidence.source: Simply Wall St (Modular talks — unverified, single-sourced)

flags.headline: MARA +4.44% — downgraded RED→AMBER: same sector-wide miner rally, BTC exposure unresolved
flags.detail: Rose on the same sector-wide spillover from the TeraWulf-Anthropic lease news, not a MARA-specific catalyst; coverage recirculated the already-known Citizens JMP Outperform/$24 initiation (originally dated 2026-06-24) rather than a new rating action. A Form 4 showed CEO Fred Thiel had 63,101 shares withheld at $13.89 for RSU tax purposes on vesting — routine, not an open-market sale. Bitcoin itself was soft/mixed the same session. Downgrading on lack of new negative catalyst and price stabilization, not on improved fundamentals — the core thesis risk (MARA as a leveraged derivative of Bitcoin price) is unchanged.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MARA key_risk: "Revenue concentration in Bitcoin mining means MARA's financial performance is essentially a leveraged derivative of Bitcoin price."

flags.headline: FTNT +3.90% — persisting AMBER, unchanged: FortiBleed reporting static since 7/5, no confirmed customer/analyst impact
flags.detail: No material new development since 2026-07-05. Fortinet's only official statement remains its PSIRT blog post (originally 2026-06-19) stating this is not a new Fortinet vulnerability and that it is proactively contacting affected customers. The Hacker News' INC/Lynx ransomware linkage (via SOCRadar, 2026-07-02) is unchanged, not new. Device-count estimates remain inconsistent (CISA and most named vendors: ~73,000-86,000; some aggregator sites claim up to 430,000 — that high-end figure traces to low-quality SEO content, not tier-1, and should be disregarded absent corroboration from CISA, Fortinet, or a named research firm). No analyst downgrade or confirmed customer churn found. Price rose +3.90% today with the broader tech tape — no negative market reaction. Holding at AMBER pending a name-specific impact signal.

flags.headline: KEYS +1.96% — downgraded RED→AMBER: partial recovery continues, fundamentals never wavered
flags.detail: Recovering in the broad chip/AI-capex-fear unwind; no new tier-1 news found dated 7/6-7/7 (Keysight newsroom, investor releases, Yahoo/Seeking Alpha all checked). Fundamentals remain intact (Q2 revenue +31%, record $2.7B order backlog, new WIN Semiconductor GaN MMIC collaboration from 6/30). Next earnings 2026-08-18. Downgrading given the continued absence of any name-specific negative catalyst and a partial price recovery — this always read as valuation compression sympathetic to sector-wide fear, not a thesis break.
flags.thesis_link: Matches KEYS key_risk: "Valuation vulnerability at 49x trailing P/E ... any moderation in AI infrastructure capex could trigger significant multiple compression."

flags.headline: MRVL +1.52% — downgraded RED→AMBER: stabilizing back near the $250 level, no new tier-1 news
flags.detail: No name-specific tier-1 news dated 7/6-7/7 found. Price recovered modestly to $249.20, essentially retesting the $250 technical level it broke below on 7/2. Fundamentals unchanged (FY2028 $16.5B revenue target, 1.6T electro-optics transition intact); valuation (94.2x trailing) still rich vs. ~55.9x peer average. Downgrading on stabilization and absence of any confirmed negative development — same sentiment-air-pocket read as before.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MRVL key_risk: "any miss against the $16.5B FY2028 revenue target or moderation in hyperscaler AI capex would trigger severe multiple compression."

flags.headline: LRCX -0.53% — downgraded RED→AMBER: flat while chip peers rallied hard; CEO disclosed $11.7M stock sale
flags.detail: Notably did NOT participate in the broad 7/6 chip-sector rebound that lifted CRDO (+9.71%), AMD (+6.56%), QCOM (+5.87%), KEYS (+1.96%), and MRVL (+1.52%) — it was roughly flat (-0.53%). Newly disclosed: CEO Timothy Archer's Form 4 shows an $11.7M sale (30,000 shares, trade date 7/2) — a routine-cadence disclosure, not itself a red flag, but notable given the stock's relative underperformance versus peers. No new fundamental catalyst found; earnings 2026-07-29. Downgrading from RED given no further deterioration and the original move was explicitly a sentiment/valuation air-pocket, not a confirmed demand break — but flagging the divergence from peers as a watch item.
flags.thesis_link: Matches LRCX key_risk: "any deceleration in AI infrastructure spending ... could trigger significant multiple compression" at a 36.55x forward P/E.

flags.headline: CRDO +9.71% — RESOLVED: fresh sell-side upgrades (Evercore, Stifel, BofA) fully reverse the AI-capex-fear selloff
flags.detail: Surged on 2026-07-06 after Evercore ISI initiated at Outperform ($325 PT), Stifel raised its target to $350 (Buy), and BofA raised to $340 — all citing AI-connectivity growth, more than reversing the prior -6.66% drop. Insider-selling watch item: the latest Form 4s show a smaller, lower-cadence pattern (director Clyde Hosein sold 3,451 shares on 7/1; COO Lam Yat Tung had 6,361 shares withheld for RSU taxes on 7/1 and 7/5, routine, not open-market sales) versus the 123-disposition/$20M+ pattern through 6/26 — an apparent easing, though one data point isn't enough to call the pattern resolved; kept as a low-grade watch item, not a flag.

flags.headline: AMD +6.56% — RESOLVED: Goldman raises PT to $640 (from $450), Citi adds to upside catalyst watch
flags.detail: Jumped ~7.5% on 2026-07-06 after Goldman Sachs raised its price target to $640 (Buy reiterated); Citi added AMD to its upside catalyst watch citing durable AI demand. Secondary positive data points: Japanese AI startup Turing said ~10% of its training workload shifted from Nvidia to AMD, and Nvidia's competing Kyber NVL144 rack system was reported delayed to 2028. MI450/Helios ramp and Q2 guidance ($11.2B, +46% YoY) remain intact; 'Advancing AI 2026' event confirmed for 2026-07-23.

flags.headline: LMT -1.49% — CONFIRMED: definitive agreement to acquire Ultra Maritime for $3.45B (was rumor-stage as of 7/2)
flags.detail: Lockheed Martin announced on 2026-07-06 a definitive agreement to acquire Ultra Maritime from Advent International for $3.45B (undersea/anti-submarine warfare: sonar, sonobuoys, torpedo-defense systems), joining LMT's Rotary and Mission Systems segment; Citi advised LMT. This confirms the FT frontrunner reporting from 2026-07-02. At LMT's ~$110B market cap this is a targeted, not transformative, bolt-on. Stock was down -1.49% today despite the confirmation — reads as broad dividend-sleeve rotation on a risk-on day (see summary) rather than a reaction to the deal itself.

evidence.source: Financial Times (via Yahoo Finance, original frontrunner report)

flags.headline: GPC -2.94% — persisting INFO: NAPA/O'Reilly bid decision still pending; next hard catalyst Q2 earnings 7/21
flags.detail: No decision reached; situation unchanged since the 2026-07-02 report of O'Reilly's ~$10B+ cash bid for GPC's automotive/NAPA unit. Stock pulled back -2.94% today (giving back a small part of its prior +12.91% pop), consistent with broad dividend-sleeve rotation on a risk-on day, not new negative information. GPC's Q2 2026 earnings are confirmed for 2026-07-21 — the next hard catalyst for an update on the sale-vs-spinoff decision (still targeted 'by end of summer').
flags.thesis_link: Directly relevant to GPC key_risk ("business separation execution risk") and key_catalyst ("Planned separation of automotive/industrial businesses ... potentially unlocking $5-10B+ in value").

flags.headline: HOOD +4.35% — informational: Robinhood Chain mainnet formally launched, London keynote 7/3
flags.detail: Robinhood Chain (Arbitrum-based L2) went live on public mainnet 2026-07-01 and was formally unveiled at Robinhood's 'The World is Flat' London keynote on 2026-07-03 — Stock Tokens now live in 120+ countries, plus DeFi lending (Robinhood Earn, ~7% APY on USDG, insured via Lloyd's of London/RELM) with partners Uniswap, Alchemy, BitGo, and Chainlink.

flags.headline: COIN +2.06% — informational: 'Open USD' stablecoin consortium reporting continues, still not tier-1-confirmed
flags.detail: Multiple crypto-trade-press outlets (Engadget, CryptoSlate, thirdweb) report Coinbase joined the 'Open USD' (OUSD) consortium as a launch partner alongside Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, BlackRock and 130+ others (dated 7/4-7/5); Circle's stock reportedly fell 17% on the news. No Reuters/Bloomberg/WSJ coverage or a Coinbase 8-K confirming participation was found — remains unconfirmed by a tier-1 source per the original framing.
